newsitem.title: USA: NRC proposes $100,000 fine for Com Ed plant.
newsitem.headline: NRC proposes $100,000 fine for Com Ed plant.

text.p: The staff of the Nuclear Regulatory Commission Friday recommended fining Commonwealth Edison, a unit of Unicom Corp, $100,000 for engineering and maintenance violations at the company's Byron nuclear power plant.

The utility was cited for failing to properly use design information to test and operate a cooling water system for safety-related equipment at the plant, the NRC said. Com Ed also failed to correct maintenance problems with the system for three years, the NRC said in a statement.
Commonwealth Edison officials were not immediately available for comment on the proposed fine.

The NRC said the company has until March 29 to either pay the fine or file a protest. The utility may request a hearing if the fine is protested and subsequently imposed by the NRC staff, the agency said.
Later, Commonwealth Edison said the issues cited by the NRC were discussed in a January 24 meeting.

"Byron Station remains one of the most highly regarded and safest generating stations in the U.S.," Ken Graesser, Byron Station vice president, said in a statement. "The station is resolved to learn from this experience."
The utility did not directly address whether it will pay the $100,000 fine or file a protest, although a spokesman said the company has 30 days to review the fine recommendation.
The NRC had cited problems in removing silt from the basins of the plant's cooling towers, a situation Com Ed said it acknowledged in one of its reports.
Unicom shares were trading up 1/4 Friday at 22-1/8.
